lessons.lesson: Claims marked 'Carried from v1.1.1' in evidence.json survived two audits without re-verification, and two of them were wrong: the SaaS-regions claim (factually inverted) and the api-reference API-key phrasing (understated a completed EOL, and contradicted SKILL.md's own correct text). An inherited medium-high-confidence claim is the HIGHEST-risk category in the file, not the lowest, because its confidence label suppresses scrutiny. Re-verify carried claims against source on every pass.

Three defects were only findable by running the binary: `jf scan --format=spdx` (rejected outright), `jf audit --fail --min-severity=High` (evaluates no policy without --watches/--project/--repo-path, so it is a security gate that gates nothing), and `jf docker scan --format` not accepting cyclonedx unlike `jf scan`. All three read as plausible. Download the pinned CLI version and run --help on every flag the skill cites.

mycompany.jfrog.io looked like an inert placeholder but resolves to a real deactivated JFrog SaaS tenant that 302s to a reactivation landing page. Any reader pasting a token into the curl examples would send a Bearer token to a third-party reclaimable host. Vendor-suffixed placeholders (*.jfrog.io, *.atlassian.net, *.myshopify.com) are wildcard-routed namespaces; curl and dig them, and prefer the vendor's own documented placeholder (acme.*).

The Hugging Face 'deprecates in June 2026' gotcha was correct when written and became wrong purely from the passage of time. Any gotcha phrased as a future deadline flips meaning at the deadline. Grep for future-tense dates on every pass and rewrite past-due ones as incident conditions.

Of five Israel-flavored gotchas, one was factually inverted, one fabricated, and two were generic filler that would read identically in any directory skill (Sunday-Thursday deploy cycles, SSO with Azure AD). A real Israeli angle changes a decision. Here the strongest available ones were sitting unused: JFrog is an Israeli company (Netanya, NASDAQ FROG), and JFrog Cloud has three Israeli regions.

evidence.json used a legacy schema (claim/source/confidence/evidence) that the gate does not read; the canonical fields are claim_id/claim/source_url/raw_snippet/fetched_at/appears_in. Because the field names never matched, verify-evidence.py had NEVER actually run on this skill, which is the most likely reason three fabrications reached production. A gate that silently no-ops is worse than no gate: it produces the confidence of verification without the fact. Check that the gate reports a non-zero extracted-claim count, not just that it exits 0.

jfrog.com/help/r/jfrog-release-information/pipelines-end-of-life returns HTTP 200 but serves a legacydocs DIRECTORY INDEX listing PDFs, not an EOL page. A status-code-only link check passes it forever. Soft-404s need a content assertion: fetch the page and confirm it contains a term from the claim it is cited for. Found only because --check-sources reads the body.

I put a 'verbatim' Frogbot V2 sunset quote in evidence.json that I had taken from a WebSearch result summary, not from reading the page. --check-sources caught it: the sentence is not on docs.jfrog.com/security/docs/frogbot at all. The real text is on the GitHub README ('V2 (v2_main branch) is in sunset mode...'). The claim was right and the attribution was wrong, which is exactly the failure mode that makes a fabricated snippet dangerous: it passes the gate while asserting something false. Only ever paste raw_snippet from bytes you fetched yourself.

Chasing a real snippet for the CBOM claim disproved part of it. The Xray release notes say only 'Added support for exporting Secrets scan results in CycloneDX (CBOM) format.' The words 'Cryptography Bill of Materials' appear nowhere on the page, certificates are not mentioned, and the entry could not be pinned to 3.131. The skill had asserted all three. Forcing yourself to find a verbatim snippet is itself a fact-check: if you cannot find text that says what you wrote, you did not have the fact.

jfrog.com/help/r/* is a Fluid Topics SPA: curl and even document.body see only nav chrome, and the doc content is not in the iframe DOM either. The readable path is the page's own content API (/help/api/khub/maps/<mapId>/pages), discoverable from performance.getEntriesByType('resource'). This is how the three Israeli cloud regions were confirmed with their AWS/Azure/GCP parents. Mark such entries verified_via=browser with verified_at.
lessons.applies_to: any skill citing jfrog.com/help or another Fluid Topics doc site

deferred_to_next_pass.note: JFrog AppTrust launched 2025-09-09 at swampUP, EIGHT MONTHS before the v1.2.0 audit, and was missed entirely. It is now a first-class CLI namespace (`jf apptrust`: app-create, version-create, version-promote, version-distribute, package bindings) plus `jf evd create-evidence` for signed in-toto DSSE attestations (ecdsa/rsa/ed25519, --sigstore-bundle, --integration sonar). This matters for Step 4: the skill teaches `jf rt build-promote` as THE promotion model, which is now the legacy path. Source: https://jfrog.com/press-room/jfrog-unveils-apptrust-devgovops-solution-to-redefine-software-release-governance/

`jf skills` (alias of `jf agent skills`): list / publish / install / update / search / delete. Artifactory is now an agent-skill registry. Unusually on-point for a skills-il directory entry and a strong Israeli-angle hook (Israeli-built skill registry). Verbatim: 'Publish a skill to Artifactory', 'Install a skill from Artifactory'.

`jf mcp install --agent=claude --global` writes the JFrog MCP server entry for Claude Code or Cursor; auth completes via OAuth in the agent so no credentials land in agent config. Endpoint is <platform-url>/mcp (`jf mcp show`). Belongs in a skill whose entire audience is agent users.

Structural gap. The skill starts AFTER setup is done: it never says how to create repositories. All four Examples are 'User says X / Result: <paragraph>' with no commands, no REST bodies, no config JSON. The local/remote/virtual model (the thing every new Artifactory user gets wrong) is buried in an appendix table. Xray indexing appears only as a troubleshooting entry when it is a prerequisite. There is no end-to-end policy -> watch -> CI-gate walkthrough. Fix with `jf setup <pkgmgr> --repo=<virtual>` plus PUT /api/repositories/{key} bodies, or narrow the description to 'reference skill'.

Absent from the skill: `jf sbom-enrich` (enrich an external Syft/CDXgen CycloneDX SBOM with Xray data), `jf curation-audit` (diagnose 403s from curation-blocked installs, the most common Curation support question), `jf hugging-face`/`jf hf upload|download` (purpose-built ML path vs the generic `jf rt upload` the skill shows), `jf exchange-oidc-token` (non-GitHub CI OIDC), `jf setup`. Partially added to references/api-reference.md this pass; not yet in SKILL.md prose.

The skill names four scanning commands across three surfaces with no guidance on which to use when. CLI help is explicit: `jf audit` resolves a dependency graph from source; `jf scan`/`jf xr scan` binary-scan built artifacts; `jf docker scan` targets a local daemon image; `jf build-scan` targets published build-info. A one-line decision table fixes the question most likely to be asked.

Pipelines hit EOL 2026-05-01 but `jf pl` still ships in CLI 2.117.0 (status, trigger, sync, sync-status, version). One clause in the EOL gotcha would stop a reader who finds the namespace from concluding the product is alive.

Unresolved, low confidence. SKILL.md says 'Administration > Identity and Access > Integrations > OIDC'; `jf exchange-oidc-token --help` says 'Admin > User Management > OIDC'. Verify in-product before changing.

The ~$27k/yr Pro X and ~$48k/yr Enterprise X self-managed figures are sourced only to third-party trackers (vendr.com is 403-blocked to automated fetches, checkthat.ai is 200). SaaS tier prices ARE verified against jfrog.com/pricing (Pro $150/mo list, currently promo $50/mo; Enterprise X from $950/mo; Enterprise+ on quote). Keep the self-managed numbers at confidence: medium or drop them.

Process lesson: the researcher reported that the AI Catalog does not cover Anthropic and that no launch date is published. Both were WRONG: the press release the skill already cites names Anthropic and Nemotron and is dated 2025-09-09. Verify a reviewer's negative claim as carefully as a positive one.

Process lesson: the Expert reported that POST /api/v2/summary/artifact needs a `default/<repo>/<path>` prefix. The v2 OpenAPI example uses a bare `docker-local/nginx/latest/manifest.json`, so the script's format was already right and 'fixing' it would have broken it.

Process lesson: the Israeli cloud-regions claim rested on a URL that now renders an empty shell. Retiring it in one bullet while a neighbouring bullet still asserted 'the in-country cloud regions above' produced a live self-contradiction that only the Judge caught. When you retire a claim, grep for every place that depends on it.
